function: p. 5-6: PPO agent jointly selects active antennas, allocates power and sets beamforming weights of a near-field ELAA to maximize the secrecy rate against eavesdroppers.
system: p. 3, 8: base station with 32x32 planar ELAA (1024 antennas), two legitimate users and two eavesdroppers with single-antenna channels implied, near-field LoS, 28 GHz, no RIS.
method: p. 6-7: PPO reinforcement learning, shared policy/value networks with Gaussian continuous and Bernoulli antenna-selection branches, ReLU, clipped objective, GAE; trained on-policy in simulation.
data_channel: p. 3-4, 8: custom free-space LoS spherical-wavefront channel (Eqs. 15-16), 28 GHz, fixed user and eavesdropper positions; no dataset, 3GPP model or measurements.
test_conditions: p. 5, 8-9: policy learned for static user positions (two users, two eavesdroppers); sweeps over transmit power, antennas used, eavesdropper distance, number and angle; no unseen-condition test stated.
baselines: p. 8: OP-NAS (all antennas), RP-OAS (random power) and far-field model FFM; OP-NAS and RP-OAS use the same PPO framework; no earlier learned or classical optimization method compared.
metrics: p. 8-9: average secrecy rate (bps/Hz) versus transmit power, percentage of selected antennas, eavesdropper distance, eavesdropper number and angular offset; reward per episode for discount factors.
complexity: none: p. 8 only states qualitatively that fewer active antennas lower complexity; no order, FLOPs, parameter count or runtime.
openness: none: no code or data link; Table I (p. 8) lists only PPO hyperparameters.
q1_support: p. 3: "adopt a free-space Line-of-Sight (LoS) channel model with" spherical-wave propagation (Eqs. 15-16, p. 4) - custom simulator; no 3GPP TR 38.901, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data is used.
q2_support: p. 5: "user positions are assumed static for simplicity" - the policy is learned for fixed locations; Figs. 2-5 only sweep power, antennas, eavesdropper distance and number; no unseen scenario, transfer or fine-tuning is reported.
q3_support: p. 8: "We compare the performance of four models." - OP-OAS (proposed), OP-NAS and RP-OAS (variants of the same PPO framework) and FFM; no earlier published learned method or other standard DRL algorithm is compared.
q4_support: p. 8: "lowers beamforming and power allocation complexity" - qualitative only; no complexity order, operations, parameter count or runtime is reported.
q5_support: p. 8: "model through numerical simulations" - own simulated setup (Table I, p. 8); no code or data link or DOI, and no public dataset, is given.
notes: Included: PPO learns the transmit beamforming weights (with antenna selection and power) of a near-field ELAA, so area 3 by function (precoder); physical-layer security is not an excluded function. Receivers are single-antenna but the transmitter has 1024 antennas, so the system check passes. The learned baselines are variants of the proposed method (OP-NAS, RP-OAS); the design method of FFM is not stated (p. 8).
